To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the in vivo imaging model based on the transient expression of luciferase in lung tissue under the control of the bovine promoter IL-8, allows to monitor in real time lung inflammatory response to bacterial infection and to evaluate the activity of anti-inflammatory compounds in the treatment of lung inflammatory diseases.
the bovine IL8 promoter is a suitable molecular read-out for the monitoring of the inflammatory response in vivo and that it can be used to evaluate the anti-inflammatory potential of new molecules.

we developed a novel in vivo imaging approach for the detection and monitoring of lung inflammation and that we used the model for the functional characterization of the pro-inflammatory capability in vivo of Pseudomonas supernatants and for the evaluation of the activity of an anti-inflammatory drug.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an innovative approach for the functional characterization of the lung inflammatory responses induced by bacterial virulence determinants.
the development of a novel in vivo imaging approach for the detection and monitoring of lung inflammation induced by bacterial virulence factor and its modulation.
the study of the pro-inflammatory capability in vivo of bacterial virulence elements and with the identification of new anti-inflammatory drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this model could be used to evaluate the anti-inflammatory activity and the safety of new compounds, to identify the bacterial factors with pro-inflammation activity, to monitor the lung inflammatory response in vivo in the course of lung infections and to evaluate the effect of different therapeutic strategies.
this experimental model is a useful approach for monitoring in real time the in vivo inflammatory response to bacterial virulence factors.
the in vivo imaging model is a useful tool in the study of bacterial pathogenesis, particularly in the identification of virulence factors and the assessment of anti-inflammatory molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the utility of the bovine Il-8 promoter to drive the expression of luciferase in a mouse model of lung inflammation induced by bacterial virulence elements.
we developed a new in vivo imaging model for monitoring lung inflammation in response to bacterial infections and its modulation by anti-inflammatory molecules.
the in vivo imaging approach is suitable to monitor the lung inflammatory response and to functionally evaluate the anti-inflammatory activity and the efficacy of new drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of this model may be extended to other bacterial pathogens, such as Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas spp., and Streptococcus pneumoniae.

in vivo imaging of the IL-8 promoter activity in mice is a useful tool for the functional analysis of the lung inflammatory pathways and can be exploited for monitoring the anti-inflammatory activity in vivo of novel compounds and/or for the screening of new molecules with therapeutic potential.

the use of a mouse model transiently expressing a luciferase reporter under the control of the bovine promoter is an efficient approach for monitoring the lung inflammatory response and for evaluating the activity of anti-inflammatory compounds.
